root_cause.text: In mm/shmem truncate handling, the shmem_undo_range() retry path reused indices[i] from find_get_entries() instead of the large swap entry’s rounded-down base index, so a middle-of-entry lookup caused shmem_free_swap() to keep failing on the same misaligned index and loop forever.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that when index points into the middle of a large swap entry, find_get_entries() returns the entry with indices[0] equal to that middle index, shmem_free_swap() fails because “the entry's base index will be smaller than indices[0]” due to the “base < index” check, and the code “retry with the same index,” causing “an infinite loop”; the patch fixes this by computing `base = round_down(base, 1 << order)`, checking `base < start || base + (1 << order) > end`, and retrying with `index = base` instead of `indices[i]`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In mm/shmem truncate handling, the shmem_undo_range() retry path reused indices[i] from find_get_entries() instead of the large swap entry’s rounded-down base index, so a middle-of-entry lookup caused shmem_free_swap() to keep failing on the same misaligned index and loop forever.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states that when index points into the middle of a large swap entry, find_get_entries() returns the entry with indices[0] equal to that middle index, shmem_free_swap() fails because “the entry's base index will be smaller than indices[0]” due to the “base < index” check, and the code “retry with the same index,” causing “an infinite loop”; the patch fixes this by computing `base = round_down(base, 1 << order)`, checking `base < start || base + (1 << order) > end`, and retrying with `index = base` instead of `indices[i]`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix shmem range undo to correctly align and skip large swap entries that cross either truncation boundary, retrying from the entry base when needed.
intent_record.what: The change introduces a new local variable `pgoff_t base = indices[i];`, keeps the result of `shmem_confirm_swap()` in `order`, and replaces the previous single end-boundary check `if (order > 0 && indices[i] + (1 << order) > end) continue;` with logic that, for large swap entries (`order > 0`), rounds `base` down to the aligned start of the large entry and skips processing if the entry crosses either the start boundary (`base < start`) or the end boundary (`base + (1 << order) > end`). It also changes the retry index assignment from `index = indices[i];` to `index = base;` and updates the related comments accordingly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes handling of large swap entries during range undo/truncation aware of the full extent of the entry instead of only the current index and only the end boundary. It prevents retrying on a large swap entry that partially overlaps the truncation range at either edge, and when retry is needed, it restarts from the aligned base of the large swap entry rather than a potentially interior index. This avoids incorrect reprocessing of partially covered large swap entries and correctly handles cases where an entry was replaced by a page or expanded.

grouping_result.intent: Fix shmem range undo to correctly align and skip large swap entries that cross either truncation boundary, retrying from the entry base when needed.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the shmem_undo_range retry logic for large swap entries by aligning to the entry base and handling boundary-crossing entries correctly, which matches the root cause of reusing a misaligned index and looping indefinitely.

candidates.rationale: This retry assignment is the direct root cause: it restarts from the lookup index returned by find_get_entries(), which may point into the middle of a large swap entry instead of its rounded-down base index, causing repeated failed shmem_free_swap() attempts and an infinite loop.

Using indices[i] as the starting index for freeing a swap entry is vulnerable when indices[i] is not aligned to the base of a large swap entry; this misaligned free attempt is what fails and triggers the bad retry path.

This confirmation logic also uses the possibly middle-of-entry indices[i], reinforcing the incorrect handling of large swap entries discovered via find_get_entries() rather than working from the entry base.

vuln_statements.explanation: This retry assignment is the direct cause of the infinite loop. When find_get_entries() returns an index from the middle of a large swap entry, reusing indices[i] instead of the entry's rounded-down base index causes the loop to retry the same misaligned position, so shmem_free_swap() keeps failing on the same entry.

This call initiates freeing using indices[i], which may point into the middle of a large swap entry rather than its aligned base. That misaligned free attempt fails and leads into the faulty retry path.

This confirmation step also operates on the potentially misaligned indices[i] returned by find_get_entries(), contributing to incorrect handling of large swap entries instead of resolving from the entry base.
